title: Graduation Project Thesis: AstraIPS
description: Fog-native, two-layer MQTT intrusion prevention on a Raspberry Pi 5: Snort 3 with a custom Lua preprocessor plus a BiLSTM classifier.
longDescription: AstraIPS addresses application-layer command injection threats in MQTT-based IoT networks through a fog-native, two-layer inline intrusion prevention system running on a Raspberry Pi 5. The first layer is Snort 3 with a custom MQTT-aware Lua preprocessor for protocol-aware parsing and signature detection; the second is a sequence-aware BiLSTM classifier that catches novel and obfuscated payloads. A four-stage, per-device enforcement policy escalates from flag, to alert, to packet drop, to MAC quarantine. Evaluation showed 97.7% mean 5-fold accuracy (AUC 0.991), 29 ms AI inference and only 2.5% CPU usage on the edge device. The thesis won 1st Place Overall out of 89 projects at the UOWD Research Competition (2026), and the thesis article has been accepted in IEEE Access.
impact: 29 ms AI inference at 2.5% CPU on Raspberry Pi 5
Four-stage per-device enforcement: flag, alert, drop, MAC quarantine
1st Place Overall of 89, UOWD Research Competition 2026; accepted in IEEE Access

title: From Clicks to Collision: A Cyber-Physical Kill Chain
description: Full cyber-physical kill chain against a ROS1 robot: Wi-Fi breach, SSH key theft, LiDAR spoofing and a denial-of-service shutdown. 2nd place, Hack My Robot, CSAW'25.
longDescription:
A red-team attack on an autonomous robot built for the "Hack My Robot" competition at CSAW'25 (Center for Cyber Security, NYU Abu Dhabi, 6-8 November 2025). Team Smooth Operators was selected among the 5 MENA finalists and won 2nd place. I worked with Hiba Anwar, Minteena Prajith and Sruti Pillutla (University of Wollongong in Dubai).

We demonstrated a complete three-phase kill chain that takes a remote attacker from the Wi-Fi perimeter all the way to a physical collision and total shutdown, exploiting the insecure-by-design ROS1 framework.

Phase 1 - Perimeter Breach & Credential Theft:
• Captured the WPA2 handshake (deauth + aircrack-ng) and cracked it offline with Hashcat and rockyou/SecLists
• Mapped the network with Nmap, brute-forced the operator login with Hydra and a CUPP-generated wordlist
• Located and exfiltrated the robot's unencrypted private SSH key from the operator machine (CWE-521 weak PSK, CWE-522 unprotected credentials)

Phase 2 - System Infiltration & Data Poisoning:
• Used the stolen SSH key for a root shell on the robot's onboard computer
• Joined the ROS graph as a rogue node (spoofed ROS_MASTER_URI / ROS_IP)
• Spoofed LiDAR: intercepted /scan, deleted the obstacle, and republished a falsified high-frequency scan; tampered with navigation parameters via the ROS Parameter Server (CWE-306 missing ROS1 auth, CVE-2018-10657)

Phase 3 - Operational Sabotage & Neutralization:
• Hijacked navigation goals to drive the robot into the obstacle (collision)
• Spammed AMCL global_localization to corrupt the robot's pose and cause erratic motion
• Killed the ROS Master (rosmaster) for a full denial of service - a single command because ROS1 has one central point of failure

Impact: showed how weak credentials, unauthenticated ROS1 protocols and a centralized architecture create critical safety hazards (collisions, erratic behaviour), operational downtime, and intellectual-property exposure.
image: pictures/From Clicks to Collision - Cyber-Physical Kill Chain.jpeg
impact: 2nd place, Hack My Robot, CSAW'25 (NYU Abu Dhabi)
End-to-end 3-phase kill chain on a ROS1 robot
Wi-Fi handshake crack, SSH key theft, LiDAR spoofing, ROS Master DoS

title: MACH::GO - Autonomous Vehicle (Bosch Future Mobility Challenge 2026)
description: 1:10 autonomous car (MACH V) for the Bosch Future Mobility Challenge 2026: computer-vision lane detection, traffic-sign classification and obstacle response. First Middle East team to reach the international round.

title: Batterly: Smart Pancake Printer
description: AI-assisted embedded food printer with computer vision, automated calibration and a full-stack web control app.
longDescription:
Batterly is an AI-assisted embedded printer that prints pancake batter, a non-Newtonian fluid that is hard to extrude consistently. I led the project.

Key Features & Technical Details:
• Closed-loop, vision-assisted extrusion: a camera watches the print and the controller corrects flow in real time
• Automated calibration of the extrusion and motion system
• Full-stack web control app to upload designs, start prints and monitor progress

Project Impact & Objective:
• Research paper accepted at ICSPIS 2026, Dubai: "Batterly: Closed-Loop Vision-Assisted Extrusion for Non-Newtonian Food 3D Printing"
impact: Led the team end to end

title: Smart Audio Denoising & Speech Restoration
description: Multi-stage MATLAB pipeline to remove ringtone, fire alarm, and AC noise, restoring clear speech.
longDescription:
This project focused on the practical application of digital signal processing for speech restoration. The challenge was a single audio file contaminated with three distinct and overlapping noise sources: an iPhone ringtone, a high-frequency fire alarm, and low-frequency AC fan noise. The goal was to recover the clean, intelligible speech.

Using MATLAB, a systematic, multi-step approach was designed. Each noise source was identified via time-domain and spectrogram analysis, then targeted with tailored techniques.

Key Features & Technical Details:
• Noise Cancellation via Signal Inversion: Phase-inverted the known ringtone and mixed it into the affected segment to cancel it
• Frequency-Domain Filtering for Tonal Noise: Designed precise bandstop filters to remove AC hum (≈1-400 Hz) and fire alarm tones (≈1.5 kHz and ≈3.4 kHz)
• Comparative Analysis & Visualization: Built a MATLAB dashboard with waveforms and spectrograms before/after for clear proof of improvement

Project Impact & Objective:
• Restored intelligible speech from an otherwise unusable recording
• Demonstrated proficiency in selecting the right approach (inversion vs. filtering)
• Mastered spectrogram-driven diagnosis and MATLAB Signal Processing Toolbox workflows
impact: Recovered clear speech from corrupted audio

title: Smart Agricultural Monitoring System
description: End-to-end IoT solution for real-time soil, light, and climate monitoring with cloud dashboard and email alerts.
longDescription:
This project addresses modern agriculture challenges with a data-driven remote monitoring solution. An Arduino Uno R4 WiFi aggregates sensor data (soil moisture, ambient light, temperature, humidity) and streams it to ThingSpeak for live visualization, while also logging locally.

A MATLAB script periodically analyzes daily logs to detect anomalies and dispatch email alerts.

Key Features & Technical Details:
• Centralized IoT Hub: Arduino Uno R4 WiFi (C++) polls DHT11, LDR, and soil moisture sensors at intervals
• Cloud Integration & Dashboard: Wireless telemetry to ThingSpeak enables remote, real-time graphs and gauges
• Automated Anomaly Alerts: MATLAB parses daily CSV logs; threshold breaches trigger email notifications with context
• Robust Data Logging: Dual logging to cloud and local CSV for redundancy and historical analysis

Project Impact & Objective:
• Built a complete IoT monitoring pipeline from sensor to cloud alerting
• Integrated embedded hardware with a public cloud platform
• Proactive farm management via automated anomaly detection
• Designed and implemented the physical circuit and PCB layout

title: Traffic Sign Recognition System
description: MATLAB app combining edge detection and BoF/SVM to classify traffic signs with 94% validation accuracy.
longDescription:
This project presents a complete traffic sign recognition system built within MATLAB, targeting an efficient ADAS component. Images are preprocessed using Sobel edge detection to emphasize sign shapes.

A Bag of Features (BoF) representation is then learned and fed into a multi-class SVM (fitcecoc) for classification, achieving 94% validation accuracy on GTSRB. A custom GUI wraps the workflow for dataset loading, training/validation, random testing, and external image upload.

Key Features & Technical Details:
• Machine Learning Pipeline: BoF feature extraction + multi-class SVM (fitcecoc) trained on GTSRB; 94% validation accuracy
• Edge Detection Preprocessing: Sobel gradient magnitude used to highlight boundaries and symbols before BoF
• Interactive MATLAB GUI: Dataset loading/preview, one-click training/validation, random test evaluation, and external image upload

Project Impact & Objective:
• Demonstrates a resource-efficient alternative to deep learning
• Fully functional GUI-based tool for end-to-end experimentation and testing

title: Parallel Image Processing Performance Analysis
description: Java histogram equalization benchmark comparing single-threaded vs. multiple parallel designs for speedup.
longDescription:
This project explores parallel computing to accelerate image processing, focusing on histogram equalization to enhance image contrast. A correct single-threaded baseline was implemented first, then multiple multithreaded designs were developed and rigorously benchmarked to evaluate performance on multi-core processors.

Key Features & Technical Details:
• Single-Threaded Baseline: Standard pixel-wise histogram equalization used as a reference for speedup calculation
• Parallel Design A (Shared State): Threads process different image parts while updating a shared histogram via AtomicIntegerArray; tested row-wise and interleaved-row work splitting
• Parallel Design B (Private State & Merge): Each thread builds a private histogram; partial results are merged (map-reduce style) to minimize contention
• Systematic Benchmarking: Runs repeated across thread counts (1, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10) recording average time and computing speedup (single-thread time / multi-thread time)

Project Impact & Objective:
• Implemented a classic image enhancement algorithm and multiple parallel patterns
• Quantified speedup to provide data-driven insights into trade-offs of shared vs. private state designs
• Gained practical experience with Java concurrency, atomic operations, and measurement
impact: Hands-on experience with Java concurrency primitives

title: Fault-Tolerant Data Processing & Resilient Logging System
description: Java simulation of majority voting for sensor validation and a cascading fallback logger to ensure data integrity.
longDescription:
This project simulates a safety-critical data processing environment in Java, emphasizing resilience to hardware and software failures. Two core principles underpin the design: accurate data via redundancy, and guaranteed capture via robust logging.

A triple-redundancy, majority voting scheme validates a critical sensor reading. Complementing this, a custom FileLogger implements a cascading fallback strategy to ensure events are recorded even under simulated I/O failures. A built-in test harness validates the voting logic and logger behavior across predefined cases and randomized simulation.

Key Features & Technical Details:
• Redundancy & Majority Voting: Three replicas of a critical sensor feed performMajorityVote: if two agree, accept value and log the outlier; if all differ, flag a major discrepancy and fall back to last known-good value
• Resilient Cascading Logger: Primary write to log.txt; on failure (simulated 40% chance) sequentially attempts backup files (log1.txt, log2.txt, ...); on total failure, writes a critical notice to principal_log.txt
• Systematic Testing & Simulation: Test harness covers agreement, one-outlier, all-different cases, then runs randomized loops to demonstrate behavior under uncertainty

Project Impact & Objective:
• Demonstrates practical fault tolerance in software systems
• Shows majority voting as a validation mechanism in redundant sensing
• Prevents silent data loss via multi-tier logging with clear escalation paths
• Validated through combined deterministic tests and randomized simulations
image: pictures/Fault-Tolerant Data Processing & Resilient Logging System.png
impact: Validated via tests and randomized simulation

title: A Hybrid Machine Learning Framework for Antenna Design Optimization
description: Published research integrating fuzzy clustering with supervised classification, achieving up to 99.21% accuracy.
longDescription:
This research introduces a two-stage hybrid ML framework to overcome limitations of manual threshold-based labeling in antenna design optimization. First, unsupervised Fuzzy C-Means (FCM) discovers performance clusters (Low/Medium/High) from engineered EM and geometric features (Wavelength, Normalized Patch Dimensions, Aspect Ratio, Slot-to-Patch Ratio).

Then, supervised models (KNN, Random Forest, Gradient Boosting, SVM, Naive Bayes) are trained on both the fuzzy-generated and manual labels to compare performance. The fuzzy-clustered labels yield balanced classes and markedly better results.

Key Features & Technical Details:
• Advanced Feature Engineering: EM and geometric features crafted to enrich model inputs
• Unsupervised Fuzzy Clustering (FCM): Data-driven class discovery into Low/Medium/High performance groups
• Supervised Model Suite: KNN, RF, GB, SVM, NB trained on both fuzzy and manual labels
• Comparative Analysis: KNN peaks at 99.21% with fuzzy labels; manual labels cause imbalance and degrade accuracy

Project Impact & Objective:
• Peer-reviewed publication demonstrating a superior alternative to manual labeling
• Strong evidence that unsupervised labeling produces balanced, meaningful classes
• Framework identifies high-performance antenna designs more reliably, enabling efficient optimization
image: pictures/A Hybrid Machine Learning Framework for Antenna Design Optimization.jpg

title: A Hybrid Deep Learning-Genetic Algorithm Approach for 5G Beam Selection
description: Published hybrid FFNN+GA model for 5G beam selection; boosted accuracy to 98% over standalone FFNN.
longDescription:
This research targets efficient downlink beam selection in 5G Massive MIMO, balancing accuracy and latency. Three strategies were benchmarked in a simulated LoS environment: a fast Feedforward Neural Network (FFNN), a Genetic Algorithm (GA), and a hybrid FFNN-GA model. The hybrid workflow first uses an FFNN for rapid prediction and then launches a constrained GA search in a small window around the predicted beam to refine the choice. Results were compared to the theoretical optimum (exhaustive search) to analyze accuracy-latency trade-offs.

Key Features & Technical Details
• Standalone FFNN Baseline: 87.65% accuracy with ~55 µs per-sample latency for real-time suitability.
• Novel Hybrid FFNN-GA: FFNN narrows the search; GA refines within a small codebook window to reach 98.00% accuracy.
• Trade-off Analysis: For a small 36-beam codebook, GA overhead can exceed exhaustive search; hybrid advantages grow with larger spaces.

Project Impact & Objective
• Peer-reviewed publication advancing AI for 5G telecommunications.
• Designed a hybrid DL-GA framework that outperforms single-model baselines.
• Delivered a clear, data-driven analysis of accuracy vs. latency for different operating regimes.
image: pictures/A Hybrid Deep Learning-Genetic Algorithm Approach for 5G Beam Selection.jpg

title: Machine Learning Framework for VANET Intrusion Detection
description: Published ML framework for VANET security with enhanced K-means and classifier benchmarking; high detection, low false positives.
longDescription:
As Vehicular Ad-Hoc Networks (VANETs) grow, so do cyber threats. This research presents a practical ML-based IDS that detects and classifies attacks (e.g., DDoS, Replay, Sybil) from traffic features. A novel, enhanced K-means clustering algorithm provides robust, data-driven grouping; supervised classifiers are then benchmarked to identify top detection models. Experiments on public datasets ensure repeatability and verification.

Key Features & Technical Details
• Enhanced K-means Clustering: Deterministic, two-step centroid initialization for improved accuracy; clusters formed using KPIs like PDR, Jitter, Throughput.
• Intelligent Attack Labeling: Cluster MSE analysis maps clusters to attack types; high-MSE clusters flagged as likely DDoS, stable clusters mapped to normal/Sybil, etc.
• Classifier Benchmarking: Models including Random Forest, MLP, J48, REP Tree, Naive Bayes trained and evaluated with TPR/FPR per attack type.
• Superior Performance: J48 and Random Forest lead with average TPR ≈ 0.88 and very low FPR, balancing detection and false alarms.

Project Impact & Objective
• Peer-reviewed publication proposing a verifiable, high-performance IDS for VANETs.
• Enhanced K-means tailored to network traffic anomaly detection.
• Rigorous model comparison to select effective classifiers for deployment.
image: pictures/Machine Learning Framework for VANET Intrusion Detection.png

title: Hardware-Accelerated Intrusion Detection System for VANETs
description: Real-time VANET IDS on Raspberry Pi 5 using Random Forest (99.72% accuracy) with protocol benchmarking (MQTT, CoAP, AMQP, TCP, UDP).
longDescription:
This practical project implements a real-time IDS for VANETs on Raspberry Pi 5, moving beyond pure simulation. Multiple ad hoc WiFi nodes simulate vehicles publishing via MQTT. A central subscriber intercepts traffic and classifies messages in real time using a trained ML model. Two investigations were conducted: selecting the most accurate ML model and benchmarking five communication protocols for suitability.

Key Features & Technical Details
• Hardware-in-the-Loop Simulation: Raspberry Pi 5 with six USB WiFi modules forms a realistic ad hoc wireless network to evaluate CPU/memory, latency, and jitter on constrained hardware.
• High-Accuracy IDS Model: Random Forest trained on NSL-KDD achieved 99.72% accuracy (Precision 99.18%, Recall 99.55%), classifying multiple attack types (DoS, Probe, R2L, etc.).
• Protocol Benchmarking: MQTT, CoAP, AMQP, TCP, UDP evaluated across 1-6 clients; MQTT provided the best balance of latency, jitter, resource use, and scalability.

Project Impact & Objective
• Built a complete hardware+software IDS prototype for VANETs.
• Delivered state-of-the-art detection accuracy and a data-driven protocol recommendation (MQTT).
• Under peer review, underscoring novelty and practical significance.
image: pictures/Hardware-Accelerated Intrusion Detection System for VANETs.png
impact: Physical VANET IDS prototype on Raspberry Pi 5
MQTT identified as optimal protocol via benchmark

title: Smart IoT Parking Management System (SmartSpot)
description: End-to-end smart parking using ESP32 sensors and a Python NPR pipeline; real-time cloud dashboard with 92% accuracy.
longDescription:
SmartSpot is a prototype-to-production smart parking solution integrating hardware, intelligent software, and cloud services. An ESP32 manages on-site edge hardware (HC-SR04 ultrasonic sensors, barrier servos, OLED display) while a host computer runs a Python-based Number Plate Recognition (NPR) pipeline using OpenCV, EAST text detection, and pyTesseract OCR. A custom debouncing state machine requires consistent plate reads for ~1.3s to slash false positives from ~25% to <2%. All events (entries/exits, bay occupancy) are logged to Google Sheets via gspread and visualized on a live web dashboard, including history search and heatmaps. The project progressed from breadboard to a KiCad-designed PCB, demonstrating a full lifecycle.

Key Features & Technical Details
• Intelligent NPR: OpenCV + EAST + pyTesseract with a debounced acceptance state machine (<2% false positives).
• Distributed Architecture: ESP32 handles real-time control; host PC runs compute-heavy NPR to keep the edge responsive.
• Real-Time Cloud & Dashboard: Instant Google Sheets logging powers a live web dashboard with analytics.
• From Prototype to PCB: Evolved from breadboard to custom KiCad PCB for robust deployment.

Project Impact & Objective
• Designed and validated an advanced, user-centric smart parking system.
• 92% first-try NPR accuracy under ideal conditions.
• End-to-end latency measured at ~1.8-2.5s from stop to barrier open.
• Complete physical prototype across embedded, CV, and cloud.

title: Autonomous Waste Collection Robot (ERC 2025)
description: ROS-based autonomous UGV with deep-learning vision and a custom forklift-style mechanism for trash collection.
longDescription:
Built for the Engineering Robotics Challenge (ERC 2025) at the American University of Sharjah, where it won the Best Poster/Design Award, this is an end-to-end autonomous UGV that navigates, detects waste, collects it, and deposits into bins. ROS provides the core navigation (gmapping SLAM, amcl localization, move_base planning/avoidance with 2D LiDAR). A fine-tuned MobileNetV2 model (TensorFlow/Keras) performs real-time detection; images are preprocessed (BGR to HSV) for robust color separation. A custom, forklift-inspired lifting mechanism engineered from LEGO Technic, a repurposed continuous track, DC motors, and an H-Bridge delivers stable scoop, lift, and deposit operations. Custom ROS nodes integrate perception, navigation, and actuation: detections are published; a control node consumes them, sends goals to move_base, and actuates the lifter to complete pickup and disposal autonomously.

Key Features & Technical Details
• Autonomous Navigation & Mapping (ROS): gmapping SLAM, amcl localization, and move_base path planning/avoidance using 2D LiDAR.
• Deep Learning Vision: MobileNetV2 real-time detection pipeline with HSV preprocessing for robust color segmentation.
• Custom Forklift Mechanism: Iteratively designed lifting system offering stability and load management under DC motor control.
• Full System Integration: ROS nodes bridge perception→navigation→manipulation for closed-loop autonomous collection.

Project Impact & Objective
• End-to-end system integrating navigation, perception, and manipulation.
• Robust ROS nav stack operation in dynamic environments.
• Reliable lifting mechanism after iterative mechanical design.
• AI-driven sorting of detected waste items.

title: Digital Currency Exchange Calculator
description: Digital logic circuit in Multisim performing currency conversion with a custom 4x4 multiplier and optimized routing.
longDescription:
This project designed, implemented, and simulated a combinational logic circuit for hardware-only currency exchange computations. Built in Multisim from standard logic gates, it accepts a 4-bit USD amount and a 2-bit selector for target currency (AED, SEK, HKD, NZD), then outputs an 8-bit converted value. Subsystems include input switches, a 2-to-4 decoder, routing logic, a hand-built 4x4 binary multiplier from Half/Full Adders, and output probes, integrated into a cohesive system for real-time observation.

Key Features & Technical Details
• Custom 4x4 Binary Multiplier: Constructed from Half Adders and Full Adders; generates partial products and sums them to produce the final result.
• Optimized Routing Mechanism: A 2-to-4 decoder and AND/OR gating select a hard-coded conversion rate into a shared multiplier, avoiding four separate multipliers and reducing gate count.
• Complete System Integration: Inputs, decoder, routing, multiplier, and output probes integrated and simulated in Multisim for interactive testing.

Project Impact & Objective
• Demonstrated practical digital design by building complex arithmetic from basic components.
• Engineered hardware reuse via routing to minimize complexity.
• Gained hands-on proficiency with Multisim for design, testing, and validation.
impact: Complete hardware arithmetic system in Multisim
Optimized gate count via routing and decoding

title: Touch-Controlled Class AB Power Amplifier
description: Designed, simulated, and built a touch-activated switch controlling a Class AB power amplifier from breadboard to soldered perfboard.
longDescription:
This project was a comprehensive, hands-on exploration of analog circuit design, integrating a transistor-based touch switch with a Class AB power amplifier. The workflow followed an engineering lifecycle: Multisim simulation, breadboard prototyping, and a robust final build on a soldered perfboard. A key study compared performance between the temporary breadboard and the soldered implementation.

Key Features & Technical Details
• Bipolar Transistor Touch Switch: Combined NPN/PNP stages responded to both positive and negative AC cycles (1 Hz), acting akin to a full-wave rectifier that alternately illuminated two LEDs to confirm bipolar operation.
• Class AB Power Amplifier: Built around an LM741 op-amp to target a voltage gain of −9. Used a complementary NPN/PNP transistor pair and diode biasing to minimize crossover distortion typical in Class B designs. Oscilloscope measurements confirmed ~−8.87 gain.
• System Integration & Comparison: Integrated touch switch and amplifier into a cohesive system and compared breadboard vs. soldered perfboard behavior. Breadboard exhibited distortion/instability; soldered version improved signal integrity, stability, and noise performance.

Project Impact & Objective
• Applied foundational analog theory to a multi-stage practical build.
• Completed full cycle from simulation to prototyping to soldered implementation.
• Demonstrated deep understanding of transistor/op-amp behavior and troubleshooting real issues (faulty parts, shorts, noise).
impact: Multi-stage analog system from concept to final hardware
Touch switch + Class AB amplifier integrated and validated
Measured −8.87 gain with minimized crossover distortion
Significant stability/noise improvements on soldered build

title: Autonomous Maze-Solving Robot with Light-Seeking Behavior
description: Webots e-puck robot in C that solves a maze via wall-following, logs light levels, and returns to the brightest location.
longDescription:
Designed and implemented an autonomous agent in Webots using the e-puck robot and the C API. The robot completes a two-phase mission: (1) explore and solve an unknown maze using a reactive wall-following algorithm driven by its IR distance sensors, and (2) analyze logged light sensor data to navigate back to the highest-intensity location after maze completion. The controller uses differential drive control and modular logic for sensing, actuation, and data handling.

Key Features & Technical Details
• Reactive Wall-Following Algorithm: Rule-based logic using eight IR sensors to handle four scenarios: wall ahead (turn), wall on side (follow left wall), corridor (centered forward), open path (forward with slight right bias).
• Light-Seeking with Data Logging: Continuously samples eight light sensors and stores readings with position/path context; on completion, identifies the peak intensity and drives back to that location using recorded path history.
• Webots C API Control: wb_motor_set_velocity for differential drive; wb_distance_sensor_get_value and wb_light_sensor_get_value for perception; wb_led_set for completion indication and status.

Project Impact & Objective
• Robust maze solving without a priori map using reactive control.
• Dual-objective mission combining exploration with intelligent return behavior.
• Hands-on proficiency with Webots simulation and C-based robotics development.
• Iterative debugging and modular design improved sensor logic and data handling.
image: pictures/Autonomous Maze-Solving Robot with Light-Seeking Behavior.png
impact: Implemented reliable wall-following in dynamic mazes
Logged and analyzed environmental light data
Autonomous return to brightest location using path history
Developed with Webots e-puck and C API

title: Multi-Site Enterprise Network Design & Implementation
description: Secure, scalable two-site enterprise network with IPsec VPN, DMZ, and hierarchical star topology.
longDescription:
Comprehensive redesign and implementation of a multi-office enterprise network. The architecture employs a hierarchical star topology with per-office subnets connected to a central router for scalable performance and easier management. A site-to-site IPsec VPN (ISAKMP policies, AES-256/SHA transform sets, ACL-defined interesting traffic) securely links the Dubai and Abu Dhabi offices. A dedicated DMZ hosts public-facing servers, isolating them from the trusted LAN to harden the posture. Cisco IOS configurations covered router interfaces and addressing, static and RIP routing for reachability, and multilayer switch setup to support higher traffic and future VLAN segmentation.

Key Features & Technical Details
• Hierarchical Star Topology: Structured, scalable design with subnet isolation per office.
• Secure IPsec VPN: ISAKMP policy, AES-256/SHA transforms, ACLs for encrypted inter-office traffic.
• Multi-Zone Security (DMZ): Public server segment isolated from internal LAN.
• Cisco IOS Configuration: Router interface/IP setup, static + RIP routing, multilayer switch configuration.

Project Impact & Objective
• Replaced an outdated network with a secure, high-performance foundation.
• Seamless, protected collaboration between sites via VPN.
• Hardened infrastructure with segmentation and DMZ.
• Prepared for cloud (Azure) and future VoIP rollout.

title: Voice-Controlled Chair
description: Assistive voice-controlled chair built on Arduino and Raspberry Pi; I led the team and owned the electrical design.
longDescription:
An assistive chair that moves on voice commands, built for people with limited mobility. I led the team and owned the electrical design.

Key Features & Technical Details:
• Voice command recognition on a Raspberry Pi
• Arduino motor control and sensor integration
• Full electrical design: power, motor drivers and wiring

Project Impact & Objective:
• Working assistive prototype controlled entirely by voice
